lines.text: Forty for a bag of seed. Forty.
And you charge forty for a NAIL, Gideon. One nail. I've seen the nail.
It was a good nail.
Oh, hello dear. Don't mind us. We've been having this argument since we were twelve.
Eleven.
He's right, eleven. Listen, if you ever get your hands on copper, bring it to him. It's the only thing that shuts him up.

after.hint: Gideon wants copper ore. The mountain rocks east of town have it.

lines.text: Three bass. Before the week's out. You can't.
I've pulled three bass out of this river before breakfast, Bram.
Not YOU. The new one. I'm betting on the new one.
...Huh. Alright. There's a pie on it. Come find me when you've got a rod in your hand.
Blueberry. The pie. In case you were wondering what you're fishing for.

after.hint: Finn and Bram have a bet on you. Talk to Finn by the river with a rod.

lines.text: I need honey. Two jars. Pip's coughing on the lectern again.
I'm OUT, Juniper. I'm always out. Hazel keeps saying so and she's right and I hate it.
Then where does a person get honey in this town?
A person builds a hive. A person with a farm. A person who is standing right there.
...Morning. Sorry. We're both a bit short on sleep and honey.

after.hint: Build a beehive on the farm (15 wood, 10 fiber) and the whole street will want honey.

lines.text: It's the same field.
It's a DIFFERENT field, Theo. It's the same field with different light.
It has no flowers. The field has flowers. I walk past it. I count them.
Then bring me flowers and I'll paint them. You never bring me flowers.
I bring you books.
...He does. He brings me books. Hello. If you've got wildflowers, I'd take them off your hands. Eight would do it.

after.hint: Lumi wants wildflowers. They grow in the long grass round the farm and the meadow.

lines.text: Hazel. Your goat was in the fountain.
She likes the fountain.
She ATE the fountain. The flowers. The flowers in the fountain.
Fence is down on the west side. Thirty wood and she stays home. You want to bring me thirty wood, Mayor?
...I'm the mayor.
Then find somebody who isn't. ...There's one.

after.hint: Hazel needs 30 wood for her fence. Chop trees on the farm or in the forest.

lines.text: You're up early.
Grumps. Orchard side. Pulling the apples down.
lines.text_gangsters: thugs. Orchard side. Pulling the apples down.

lines.text: So go deal with them. You've got a bow.
I've got a bad shoulder and a bow. Somebody with a sword could do it in an hour.
...He means you. He won't say it. He means you.
...Clear the orchard. I pay.

after.hint: Rook will pay to have the orchard cleared of grumps. Cross the north bridge with a sword.

lines.text: You've not paid for a room in nine days, Sal.
I've not slept in one in nine days. Chair's fine.
You've not eaten either. I notice things. It's my inn.
...I'll sort it.
You won't. But maybe they will. Bread, if you're feeling kind. He won't ask.

after.hint: Sal hasn't eaten. Posy sells bread, or bake it from flour.

lines.text: I'm not telling. It's a SECRET.
It's not a secret if you keep SAYING it's a secret.
Is it the clock tower? It's the clock tower.
IT'S NOT THE CLOCK TOWER. ...Hey. HEY. Do you have candy? I'd tell YOU for candy.
Don't. He'll just say 'clock tower'.

after.hint: Pip sells secrets for candy. Maple stocks candy.

lines.text: You've gone soft on the new one.
I have NOT. I've gone... reasonable. There's a difference.
You put a seed pack aside. I saw the label. It had a heart on it.
It had a HEART because it's STRAWBERRY, Posy. ...Oh, there you are, dear. Come by the store. I've put something aside.

after.hint: Maple put a seed pack aside for you. Plant strawberries this spring.

lines.text: Twenty years since it rang.
Twenty-one. I was there. My father pulled the rope.
The clapper's gone. Sold, melted, who knows. Gold would do it. A bar.
Gold. In this town.
...Someone's been to the mountain. Someone's been past the meadow. I'd ask them, if I were mayor.
I AM mayor. ...Fine. I'll ask.

after.hint: The town bell needs a gold bar. Gold ore is deep in the mine; smelt it at a furnace.

lines.text: You walked straight through the bog. Nobody walks straight through the bog.
Hut's there. Kettle's on. Don't touch the green jars. The green jars touch back.
...Witch is east. Past the dead trees. She's not mine. Don't bring her here.

after.hint: Old Moss trades jars and lore. The Marsh Witch waits east of the dead trees.

lines.text: Stop. You're standing on a seam.
Thirty years in this quarry, nine of them foreman, and the only thing that ever came up out of that pit was trouble and copper. Mostly trouble.
You want ore, mine it. You want the big one, the crowned one... don't. Or do. I'll be in the office either way.

after.hint: Granite sells ore and dynamite in the quarry office. The Golem King sleeps in the pit.
